sentences.text: As per the prosecution case, prior to the incident, the prosecutrix and the applicant/accused knew each other and there was love affection between them.
On 09.12.2022, the prosecutrix went to Bhopal from Ujjain alongwith the applicant.
Thereafter, both of them had gone Surat (Gujrat) and they were living in a rented house, they lived there for two months.
Meantime, the applicant had developed sexual intercourse with her.
03. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has not committed the offence and has falsely been implicated in the case.
He further submits that at the time of the incident, the prosecutrix was aged about more than 18 years.

Though, her date of birth is mentioned as 04.08.2006, but the Assistant Teacher (PW-5) in paragraph 4 of his cross-examination has admitted the fact that there was an over writing in the year of her date of birth and the date of birth written in figure was by different ink.
Therefore, scholar register is not reliable and the prosecutrix was a consenting party.
The applicant has not committed the offence and he is in custody since 31.01.2023.
Trial will take sufficient long time for its disposal, therefore, it is prayed that the present applicant be released on bail.
04. Learned Government Advocate for the State has objected the prayer and prayed for rejection of the application.
05. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

06. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, coupled with the fact that trial of the case will take sufficient long time, without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
Hence, the application is allowed.

07. It is directed that the applicant- Suresh Kumar be released on bail upon his/her furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Fifty Thousand only) with two solvent surety, out of which one shall be local surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for his/her appearance before the trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the trial Court during pendency of the trial.

It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
08.
This application is allowed and stands disposed off.
C.c. as per rules.

(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE Shilpa Suresh Kumar Solanki vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66930786/
